patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Five9 and OpenPhone share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Five9 and OpenPhone share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose Five9 only if your buying job matches “Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital from $119/concurrent seat/mo; Core $159; Plus/Pro/E” rather than OpenPhone's shape. Choose OpenPhone only if your buying job matches “Modern SMB shared business phone (also branded Quo) with shared numbers, SMS and Sona AI —” rather than Five9's shape. Workflow advantage: Five9 leans contact-center, customer-messaging; OpenPhone leans business-phone, team-communication. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Five9 and OpenPhone share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Five9 is Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital from $119/concurrent seat/mo; Core $159; Plus/Pro/Enterprise quote — 50-seat minimum.; OpenPhone is Modern SMB shared business phone (also branded Quo) with shared numbers, SMS and Sona AI — Starter from $15/user/month annual..
- Company-size focus: Five9 (mid-market, enterprise) vs OpenPhone (solo, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Five9-leaning contact-center, customer-messaging vs OpenPhone-leaning business-phone, team-communication.
- Researched limits: Five9 — 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers; OpenPhone — US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story.

Limitations — Five9: 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers; Digital is non-voice; Core is the published voice+digital entry; OpenPhone: US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story; Phone menus, automatic recording and deeper CRM require Business or above.

Poor-fit cases: Five9 is a poor fit when that limitation bites: 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers · OpenPhone is a poor fit when that limitation bites: US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story · Avoid Five9 if you actually need OpenPhone's motion (Modern SMB shared business phone (also branded Quo) with shared numbers, SMS and)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
